nodes.procedure: The washed NFF (1 cm × 1 cm, sonicated sequentially in ethanol, 6 M HCl aqueous solution, and DI water for 5 min each), Pt plate, and saturated calomel electrode (SCE) were assigned as working, counter, and reference electrodes, respectively. x mmol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, and Co(NO3)2·6H2O and Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (15 - 2x mmol) were dissolved in 100 mL DI water to form an aqueous solution. The electrodeposition process was conducted under room temperature in a potential range from -1.2 to -0.8 V (vs. SCE) for 1000 cycles at a scan rate of 50 mV/s. After the deposition, the prepared samples were dried for 6 h at 60°C.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show all pristine catalysts are mainly (oxy)hydroxides. Fe₇.₅Co₇.₅OᵧHᵤ@NFF is highly correlated with standard peaks of Ni(OH)₂·0.75H₂O, NiOOH, and FeO(OH). After OER testing, NiOOH (PDF#97-016-5961) appears as a new phase, especially prominent in Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF, indicating surface-reconstructed NiOOH is the real active layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns show that all pristine catalysts are mainly (oxy)hydroxides ... NiOOH (PDF#97-016-5961) is observed in the XRD patterns as the new phase after the OER process ... indicating that surface-reconstructed NiOOH is the real active layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show all pristine samples consist of nanoflowers assembled from nanosheets with small size and thickness. After OER testing, samples maintain similar morphology with homogeneous small-size nanoflowers assembled by nanosheets, confirming excellent structural stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface morphologies of all pristine samples consist of nanoflowers assembled from nanosheets ... the SEM images of all samples show a similar morphology with the homogeneous small-size nanoflowers assembled by nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM and HRTEM images of Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF show the catalyst is composed of nano-flower petals assembled with a compact array of nanosheets. HRTEM reveals interplanar spacing of 0.26 nm consistent with Ni(OH)₂·0.75H₂O (012).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images were taken to characterize the morphology ... the HRTEM image shows that the interplanar spacing of the pristine Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF is 0.26 nm, consistent with Ni(OH)₂·0.75H₂O(012).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images of Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF after OER testing show interplanar spacings of 0.26 nm and 0.221 nm, consistent with Ni(OH)₂·0.75H₂O(012) and NiOOH(112), providing evidence for NiOOH formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the HRTEM images show that the interplanar spacings of Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF after the OER test are 0.26 and 0.221 nm, consistent with Ni(OH)₂·0.75H₂O(012) and NiOOH(112), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF confirms the interplanar spacing of 0.26 nm consistent with Ni(OH)₂·0.75H₂O(012).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) (Figure 1D) ... consistent with Ni(OH)₂·0.75H₂O(012), which can be further confirmed by the selected area electron diffraction (SAED).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) and corresponding EDS images confirm uniform distribution of all elements (Fe, Co, Ni, and O) in Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) and corresponding EDS images confirm a uniform distribution of all elements, including Fe, Co, Ni, and O, in Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mappings confirm uniform distribution of all elements in all samples. After OER testing, Ni concentrations increase compared to pristine catalysts, implying Ni compound is the key active site. Iron content drops significantly for high-Fe-based catalysts after OER due to dissolution at high potentials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) mappings confirm that all the elements are uniformly distributed in the samples ... the EDS results show that the Ni concentrations of all samples are increased after the OER test compared to the surface components of the pristine catalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS spectra show Fe, Co, Ni, and O elements present in all pristine samples except Ni₁₅OᵧHᵤ@NFF (no Co). Fine spectra show four 2p₃/₂ peaks assignable to M²⁺, M³⁺, and satellite peaks. O 1s spectra show four peaks related to M-O, M-OH, M-OOH, and adsorbed H₂O. Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF has highest binding energy among pristine samples and smallest O 1s binding energy, indicating partial electron transfer from M to O. After OER testing, larger peak areas of Co³⁺, Ni³⁺, and M-OOH/OH indicate abundant metallic ions with high-charge states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fine Fe 2p, Co 2p, and Ni 2p spectra ... show four 2p₂/₃ peaks, which can be assigned to M²⁺, M³⁺, and corresponding satellite peaks ... the XPS results show that the Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF after the OER test has larger peak areas of Co³⁺, Ni³⁺, and M-OOH/OH than other samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry reveals significant discrepancy between original catalyst composition and electrolyte composition, providing understanding of corrosion of Ni and Fe components through solution and self-supported electrode formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry test revealed a significant discrepancy between the original catalyst composition and the electrolyte composition.

nodes.characterization_summary: Brunauer-Emmett-Teller measurements show similar surface areas for most samples except Ni₁₅OᵧHᵤ. Average pore size increases significantly as Ni content increases, illustrating importance of optimizing electrochemical deposition solution composition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We also measured the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller specific surface areas of the catalysts ... Except for Ni₁₅OᵧHᵤ, they show similar surface areas. At the same time, the average pore size of the catalyst increases significantly as the Ni content increases.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cyclic voltammetry was used for electrochemical deposition with varying cycles. Catalyst thickness increases from 16.8 to 42.1 μm as deposition cycles increase. ECSA values of samples are all above 37, greatly higher than bare NFF (27.5), indicating increased availability of active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We prepared samples via cyclic voltammetry (CV) deposition by varying the cycles. A notable increase in catalyst thickness (16.8 - 42.1 μm) is observed as the number of deposition cycles increased ... The ECSA values of the samples are all above 37 (Supporting Information S1: Figure S13G,H), greatly higher than that of NFF (27.5).

nodes.characterization_summary: Linear sweep voltammetry shows Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF requires ultra-low overpotential of 185 mV to achieve 10 mA cm⁻² in 1 M KOH, much lower than NFF (257 mV), Fe₇.₅Co₇.₅OᵧHᵤ@NFF (197 mV), Fe₅Co₅Ni₅OᵧHᵤ@NFF (181 mV), Ni₁₅OᵧHᵤ@NFF (197 mV), and RuO₂@NFF (239 mV). At high current density of 1000 mA cm⁻², Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF requires only 323 mV overpotential. Under simulated industrial conditions (6 M KOH, 60°C), Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF requires 308 mV overpotential to reach 500 mA cm⁻² with ultra-low Tafel slope of 19.7 mV dec⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Especially, the ternary metal (oxy)hydroxide catalysts show higher OER activity than other samples, requiring an ultra-low overpotential of 181 mV (Fe₅Co₅Ni₅OᵧHᵤ@NFF) and 185 mV (Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF) to achieve 10 mA cm⁻² ... In detail, it only needs 323 mV overpotential to reach a high current density of 1000 mA cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy at 1.44 V versus RHE shows charge transfer resistances (Rct) similar across samples when deposition cycles exceed 500. Sample with 1000 CV loops presents lowest Rct, suggesting efficient electron transfer. In-situ EIS from 1.38 to 1.48 V versus RHE shows Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF has smaller Rp (hindrance of Ni oxidation) and small RCT, indicating reduced energy barrier for nickel oxidation and strong OH* adsorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) curves were collected at a potential of 1.44 V versus RHE. We see that the charge transfer resistances (Rct the radius of semicircle in high-frequency region) are similar to each other when the deposition cycles exceed 500 ... The sample prepared with 1000 CV loops presents the lowest Rct in all samples, suggesting efficient electron transfer.

nodes.characterization_summary: Tafel slope analysis shows Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF exhibits small Tafel slope of 23.5 mV dec⁻¹, superior to NFF (60.0 mV dec⁻¹), Fe₇.₅Co₇.₅OᵧHᵤ@NFF (33.2 mV dec⁻¹), Fe₅Co₅Ni₅OᵧHᵤ@NFF (32.1 mV dec⁻¹), Ni₁₅OᵧHᵤ@NFF (25.7 mV dec⁻¹), and RuO₂@NFF (25.5 mV dec⁻¹), indicating excellent intrinsic OER activity and favorable reaction kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF catalyst shows a small Tafel slope of 23.5 mVdec⁻¹, which is superior to those of NFF (60.0 mVdec⁻¹), Fe₇.₅Co₇.₅OᵧHᵤ@NFF (33.2 mVdec⁻¹), Fe₅Co₅Ni₅OᵧHᵤ@NFF (32.1 mVdec⁻¹), Ni₁₅OᵧHᵤ@NFF (25.7 mVdec⁻¹), and RuO₂@NFF (25.5 mVdec⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman characterization shows all samples on NFF substrate exhibit three distinct Ni-O characteristic peaks (674, 534, and 465 cm⁻¹) except Ni₁₅OᵧHᵤ@NFF. Fe and Co-incorporated samples show red-shifted characteristic peaks and obvious NiOO⁻ peaks at 900-1100 cm⁻¹ at lower voltages, indicating Fe and Co incorporation reduces formation energy for active layer. Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF shows maximal γ-NiOOH peak intensity at 1.324 V versus RHE, lower than other samples. Intensity ratio I_δ(Ni-O)/I_ν(Ni-O) of Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF is 0.72, indicating gradual oxidation process Ni²⁺→Ni³⁺→Ni⁴⁺ rather than direct oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Fe₇.₅Co₇.₅OᵧHᵤ, the sample grown on the NFF substrate shows obvious Ni-O characteristic peaks (674, 534, and 465 cm⁻¹ corresponding to the vibration of 2p, 1p, and Ni-O bonds, respectively) ... the Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF, shows the maximal γ-NiOOH peak intensity at 1.324 V versus RHE, whereas other samples should require higher potentials to reach the maximum.

nodes.characterization_summary: Galvanostatic stability tests at 10 and 500 mA cm⁻² in 1 M KOH show Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF exhibits excellent stability with LSV curves basically overlapping after 200 h, indicating great potential for practical application. Under simulated industrial conditions (6 M KOH, 60°C, 500 mA cm⁻²), voltage increases only 8% after 1100 h continuous operation, showing ultrahigh stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe₂.₅Co₂.₅Ni₁₀OᵧHᵤ@NFF exhibits excellent stability, either at low or high current density, with the LSV curves basically overlapping after 200 h ... the voltage is only increased by 8% at 500 mA cm⁻² for continuous operation for up to 1100 h under an industrial working environment.

nodes.characterization_summary: Density-functional-theory calculations on γ-NiOOH(112) show *OH adsorption energy of ~0.11 eV and dehydrogenation as potential determining step with ΔG of ~1.80 eV. After Fe and Co incorporation as γ-(FeO,CoO)NiOOH, *OH adsorption energy increases to ~1.00 eV and PDS (formation of *OOH) ΔG decreases to 1.53 eV (~0.2 eV lower than γ-NiOOH). Electronic structure analysis shows γ-(FeO,CoO)NiOOH has expanded eg orbital, improved conductivity, and reduced band gap in spin-down channel (~1.25 eV), with higher Ni valence state due to surface O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The *OH can adsorb on the Ni ion with a Gibbs free energy change (ΔG) of ~0.11 eV ... The dehydrogenation of *OH is the potential determining step (PDS) of OER, which leads to a ΔG of ~1.80 eV ... The ΔG of the PDS (the formation of *OOH) is only 1.53 eV, which is ~0.2 eV lower than that of γ-NiOOH.
